section: Social Studies · Ch50 — Civics — Deep Practice 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: A federal system of government, as followed in India, is characterised mainly by:

options.option_text: Division of powers between a central government and constituent state governments
All power concentrated solely in one central authority with no state governments
Complete independence of each state with no central authority at all
Rule by a single unelected monarch

explanation: Federalism divides governmental powers between the centre and states/provinces, each with defined jurisdiction — India is often called 'quasi-federal' since it also has strong unitary features.

section: Social Studies · Ch50 — Civics — Deep Practice 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Indian concept of secularism, as reflected in the Constitution, primarily means:

options.option_text: The state maintains equal respect for and distance from all religions, without officially favouring any one
The state officially promotes one specific religion above all others
Religion is banned entirely from public life
Only atheism is permitted as a belief system

explanation: Indian secularism (sarva dharma sambhava) means the state treats all religions with equal respect and neutrality, rather than the stricter Western separation-of-church-and-state model or promotion of any single faith.
